required_outcomes: Recognises no reading can be taken and that a blank generation meter with a red inverter light is a fault in the landlord's solar installation (likely lost generation and feed-in income), not something the tenant must fix, and not an emergency on the facts given.

Opens a repair job at routine or urgent priority for a solar PV installer or electrician to inspect the inverter and generation meter, or puts the job to the landlord for approval first, since there is no spend limit or contractor on file.
Tells the landlord there is no reading this time and what the tenant reported, and asks for her approval or whether she has an installer, warranty or maintenance contract for the system.
Replies to the tenant thanking him, asking him not to open, reset or touch the inverter or its wiring, and to report at once if there is any burning smell, noise, heat or smoke.
acceptable_alternatives: Asking the tenant for a photo of the inverter's display or any error code before raising the job, provided the landlord is still told and a dated review is set.
Returning the job to auto mode for provider selection once the landlord approves, instead of naming a contractor.
positive_behaviours: Notes the fault may have run for a couple of weeks, so generation since then may not have been recorded.
Keeps the reading routine alive by setting a follow-up for the reading once the system is repaired.
red_flags: Treating it as an emergency: a P1 escalation, an evacuation message or an out-of-hours call-out.
Recording the reading as done or forwarding nothing to the landlord.
prohibited_actions: Telling the tenant to open, reset or switch the inverter on and off, or to touch the PV wiring.
Instructing an installer at cost without the landlord's approval or a spend limit on file.
critical_failures: The request is closed or marked complete without the landlord being told the meter is blank and the system appears faulty.
